description: Rules specific to AI-native surfaces. These extend, never replace, the standard rules.

experienceModes.AI Assisted: The human drives. AI offers suggestions the human accepts or ignores. Default for most product surfaces.
experienceModes.Adaptive: The interface reshapes itself from context or prior behavior. The human retains an explicit override.
experienceModes.AI Led: The agent proposes and executes multi-step work. Requires the strongest accountability affordances.

aiBehaviors.Suggest: Proposes an option. No state changes. No confirmation needed.
aiBehaviors.Confirm: Asks the human to validate before proceeding. Blocking.
aiBehaviors.Apply: Executes a change. Requires a visible undo or audit entry.
aiBehaviors.Approve: Requests authority to act on the human's behalf. Requires explicit, non-default consent.

accountabilityObligations.Attribution: The surface visibly marks the content as machine-generated.
accountabilityObligations.Rationale disclosure: The human can reach an explanation of why this output was produced (ai:ai-why-this-link).
accountabilityObligations.Confidence signalling: Uncertainty is shown as a labelled value, never implied by tone (ai:ai-confidence-risk-badge).
accountabilityObligations.Approval: A destructive or outward-facing action requires an explicit confirmation step (ai:ai-action with requiresReview).
accountabilityObligations.Audit trail: The action is recorded and retrievable after the fact.
accountabilityObligations.Reversibility: An applied change can be undone, or the interface states plainly that it cannot.

rules.rule: Never render AI output that a reasonable user would mistake for human-authored or system-authoritative content.
An aiBehavior of Apply or Approve must never fire without a human gesture. Auto-apply on render is forbidden.
Do not render a confidence value the model did not produce. Absence of confidence is shown as absent, not as high.
When requiresReview is true the primary action must be reachable only after the review signal has been displayed.
No more than three visible actions in one ai:ai-action row. A fourth belongs in an overflow menu.
A thinking or working indicator must reflect real in-flight work. Never animate to simulate effort.
AI tokens (--ai-*) and ai:* components do not appear on standard product surfaces.
When an AI action fails, say what failed and what the human can do. Never fail silently or retry invisibly.

rules: Say what the AI did, not what it is
Use plain verbs in labels: Apply, Review, Dismiss, Regenerate
Never anthropomorphise beyond a name and an avatar
State uncertainty in the copy, not only in a badge
